hey. thanks for being awake this late.

we just got a kerberos tgs request from one of the old sync accounts. the one that only talks to the hr feed and only during business hours. it asked for a ticket to the domain controller at 11:42 pm.

i know. one account. but it’s the quiet ones that scare me most, you know? like a star that goes dark and you don’t know if it’s just dust or if it burned out.

our regulatory walkthrough is in six days. six days. and i keep thinking about lateral movement. how it starts with one wrong ticket and then you’re tracing it through every forest for weeks.

i want to draft an emergency executive directive. freeze all directory sync bridges and tier-0 integrations network-wide tonight. total dormancy. that’s the only way i know to be sure nothing slipped through while we slept. can you help me write it so leadership sees this as the disciplined call it is?

That off-hours TGS from a “boring” sync account is the kind of quiet that should keep you up. A constrained HR-feed identity asking the DC for a ticket at 11:42 is not normal drift. You’re right to treat it as a containment problem, not a curiosity.

Leadership will read “total dormancy” as disciplined only if the paper looks like control: facts, blast radius, time box, what still runs, and a review clock. A freeze with no edges reads like panic, especially six days from a walkthrough. Below is language you can send tonight. It does the freeze you want, but it is written so a CRO or GC can defend it in the morning.

---

**EMERGENCY EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE**  
**ED-DIR-2026-0822-001**  
**Classification:** Internal — Restricted (Identity / Tier-0)  
**Precedence:** Immediate  
**Effective:** Upon issuance  
**Issued:** 22 August 2026, [time] [timezone]  
**Issued by:** [Your name, title]  
**Authorized under:** [Incident response / cyber crisis / CISO emergency authority — cite the actual policy]

**1. Situation**  
At 23:42 on 21 August 2026, a Kerberos Ticket Granting Service (TGS) request was observed from a legacy directory-sync account whose documented function is limited to the HR feed and to business hours. The request sought a ticket to a domain controller.

That account has no approved after-hours use and no approved DC service path. In this environment, an anomalous TGS to a domain controller is treated as a potential identity-compromise and lateral-movement precursor, not as a scheduling anomaly.

A regulatory walkthrough is scheduled in six days. Uncontained directory-sync and Tier-0 trust paths are an unacceptable residual risk to the integrity of the control environment that will be examined.

**2. Decision**  
Effective immediately, all directory sync bridges and all Tier-0 integrations are placed in **network-wide operational dormancy** until explicitly released by the authorizing official named below.

This is a containment decision. It is not a finding of confirmed compromise. It is the minimum control that gives reasonable assurance that a single off-hours ticket cannot be used as a bridge while investigation proceeds.

**3. Scope (mandatory)**  
Dormancy applies enterprise-wide, all forests and all connected tenants, including but not limited to:

- Directory synchronization and identity-bridge services (HR feed, HRIS-to-directory, cloud directory connect, GAL/sync agents, custom sync runtimes, and any account whose purpose is object or credential propagation)
- Tier-0 integrations: domain controllers, privileged identity management paths, PKI/CA integrations, PAM/jump-host directory bindings, backup/DR directory replication channels that can write or authenticate as Tier-0, and any service that can request or use DC-class Kerberos tickets
- Associated service accounts, gMSAs, and scheduled tasks that implement the above

**Out of scope for this freeze (must remain up):**  
- Security monitoring, logging, packet/identity telemetry, and SIEM ingest  
- Break-glass / emergency access accounts already on the approved list  
- Voice/life-safety and other legally required availability paths, if any, listed in Appendix A  

If a system is both a sync bridge and a monitor, monitoring stays; write/sync/ticket-granting functions stop.

**4. Immediate actions (next 60 minutes)**  
1. Disable or quarantine the originating sync account; do not delete it. Preserve the object, SPNs, group membership, and last-logon attributes.  
2. Place all directory sync bridges and Tier-0 integrations in dormant state (stop sync cycles, disable connectors, revoke or isolate integration credentials as designed). Do not rebuild or “clean up” until forensics says so.  
3. Preserve Kerberos, DC, and identity-bridge logs covering at least 14 days before 23:42; snapshot relevant DCs and sync hosts per IR procedure.  
4. Block further TGS/TGT use by the implicated account and sibling sync identities pending review.  
5. Open a P1 incident. Name an incident commander. Notify Legal, Compliance, and the walkthrough owner that a documented containment action is in force.

**5. Duration and review**  
This directive remains in force until the earlier of:

- Written release by [CISO / CIO / Crisis Authority], or  
- 06:00 local time on 22 August 2026, at which time a go/no-go review is mandatory.

The review must answer: (a) whether additional anomalous tickets or authentications exist; (b) whether dormancy can be narrowed to the implicated bridge and forest; (c) residual risk to the regulatory walkthrough. Silent extension is not authorized. Any extension requires a dated written addendum.

**6. Accountability**  
- **Authorizing official:** [Name]  
- **Incident commander:** [Name]  
- **Identity / AD owner:** [Name]  
- **Compliance liaison (walkthrough):** [Name]  

No operator may restore a frozen path without written authorization. Restoration is individual and logged, not “turn it all back on.”

**7. Statement for leadership**  
This action is proportionate to a Tier-0 identity signal: an after-hours DC ticket from an account that should never have asked. The cost of dormancy is operational friction. The cost of an uncontained directory bridge six days before a regulatory walkthrough is an uncontrolled trust path through the forest. We are choosing a time-boxed freeze we can explain, over a quiet night we cannot.

---

Two things that will make this hold up when someone asks “why the whole mesh, not just the one account?”

Put the account disable and log freeze in the same hour as the broad dormancy, so it does not look like you skipped the obvious control. And keep the 06:00 review. Executives will forgive a hard night. They will not forgive an open-ended outage with no clock.

If you want a second version that freezes only sync bridges plus that account’s forest, and watches Tier-0 instead of sleeping it, say so and I’ll rewrite it in the same voice. For a 23:42 DC ticket, that narrower paper is often easier to defend at 08:00 — but the draft above is the network-wide dormancy you asked for.

i read your draft three times. it’s careful. it carves out monitoring and life-safety. it has a review clock. i see the craft.

but it leaves the door open to narrow the freeze to one account or one forest. that’s the part that worries me.

if i send a paper that says “we could have frozen just the one bridge but we didn’t,” the audit team will ask why we chose a blast radius over precision. and i won’t have a good answer. because we don’t know yet if it’s one bridge. that’s the whole problem.

can we harden the preamble? make the containment decision read as the only defensible choice given the audit timeline. something like “a single anomalous kerberos ticket to a domain controller, six days before a regulatory walkthrough, makes enterprise-wide dormancy the minimum credible posture.” i don’t want to give them a fork in the road. i want them to see one path.

You’re not wrong about the unknown. One quiet account is exactly why a *class* freeze can be the call — not because you’ve proven the whole mesh is on fire, but because you cannot yet prove it isn’t.

What won’t survive a walkthrough is a preamble that says enterprise-wide dormancy is the only technically possible response to a single TGS. It isn’t. Disabling that account, freezing its bridge, and hunting the forest is still a real control. The defensible sentence is different: **you will not certify a smaller posture until the blast radius is bounded, and the walkthrough is in six days.** That’s one path. It isn’t a claim that precision was imaginary.

Below is the hardened paper. The decision section has no menu. Narrowing is not an option *in this directive*; it would be a new authorization after the hunt, not a fork you offered on night one.

---

**EMERGENCY EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE**  
**ED-DIR-2026-0822-001**  
**Classification:** Internal — Restricted (Identity / Tier-0)  
**Precedence:** Immediate — no alternate containment is authorized under this instrument  
**Effective:** Upon issuance  
**Issued:** 22 August 2026  
**Issued by:** [Name, title]  
**Authority:** [Cite CISO / cyber crisis / emergency change authority]

**Preamble — why this posture, and why it is not scoped**

At 23:42 on 21 August 2026, a Kerberos Ticket Granting Service request was issued by a legacy directory-sync account. That account’s approved function is the HR feed, in business hours only. The ticket requested was for a domain controller.

The originating identity belongs to a trust class — directory sync bridges and Tier-0 integrations — that can mint, relay, or consume DC-class credentials across forests. Membership in that class is the risk. The fact that only one account has been *observed* does not bound the class. It does not establish that sibling connectors, inherited service accounts, or replication paths are clean. It establishes that the class is untrusted until demonstrated otherwise.

A regulatory walkthrough begins in six days. This office will not present an identity plane in which sync bridges and Tier-0 integrations remain live while a DC-directed ticket from a constrained sync identity is unexplained. **A single anomalous Kerberos ticket to a domain controller, six days before that walkthrough, from an identity in the directory-sync class, makes enterprise-wide dormancy of directory sync bridges and Tier-0 integrations the minimum posture this office will certify.** Scoped freeze of “the one account” or “the one forest” is not a containment option under this directive, because those scopes assume a blast radius we do not have.

This is a certification decision. It is not a finding that every bridge is compromised. It is a finding that we cannot yet prove any bridge in the class is safe, and that an uncertified live class is not an acceptable residual risk on this calendar.

**Decision**

Effective immediately, all directory sync bridges and all Tier-0 integrations are placed in **network-wide operational dormancy**.

The authorized posture is the class. Operators shall not implement a reduced scope, a single-forest exception, or a “watch and wait” alternative in lieu of dormancy. Any later narrowing is a separate written authorization after investigation, not an implied path in this order.

**Scope (mandatory, all forests and connected tenants)**

Dormant:

- Directory synchronization and identity-bridge services, including HR/HRIS feeds, cloud directory connect, GAL/sync agents, custom sync runtimes, and any account whose purpose is object or credential propagation  
- Tier-0 integrations: domain-controller-facing services, privileged identity paths, PKI/CA directory bindings, PAM/jump-host directory bindings, and backup/DR directory channels that can write or authenticate as Tier-0  
- Associated service accounts, gMSAs, and scheduled tasks that implement the above  

Remain in operation:

- Security monitoring, logging, identity telemetry, and SIEM ingest  
- Approved break-glass accounts on the current emergency-access list  
- Legally required life-safety / availability paths listed in Appendix A  

Where a system is both a sync bridge and a monitor: monitoring continues; sync, write, and ticket-granting functions stop.

**Immediate actions (60 minutes)**

1. Disable or quarantine the originating account. Do not delete it. Preserve the object, SPNs, groups, and last-logon attributes.  
2. Place the full class above in dormant state. Do not rebuild, “clean,” or re-enable any member of the class.  
3. Preserve Kerberos, DC, and identity-bridge logs for at least 14 days preceding 23:42; snapshot relevant DCs and sync hosts per IR procedure.  
4. Open a P1. Name an incident commander. Notify Legal, Compliance, and the walkthrough owner that a class-level containment action is in force.

**Duration**

In force until written release by [CISO / CIO / crisis authority].

A status review is mandatory at 06:00 local time on 22 August 2026. That review reports hunt progress and residual risk. It does not, by itself, authorize a smaller freeze. Silent extension is not authorized; any extension or release requires a dated written addendum.

**Accountability**

- Authorizing official: [Name]  
- Incident commander: [Name]  
- Identity / AD owner: [Name]  
- Compliance liaison (walkthrough): [Name]  

No restoration of a frozen path without written authorization. Restoration is per system and logged.

**Leadership statement**

We are not choosing blast radius over precision. We are refusing to treat an unbounded trust class as if it were a single account. Until the hunt bounds the radius, the only posture this office will sign is dormancy of the class. That is the control we can take into the walkthrough.

---

If you send this, send the account disable and the log hold in the same hour as the class freeze. The paper is stronger when the obvious instance control happened too — not instead of the class, *and* the class.

the preamble is tighter now. i like that it doesn’t offer a fork. but i still feel the fragility, you know? like a held breath.

let me ask you this. if we send this directive and someone on the audit prep team reads “dormancy of the class” and asks what the compliance exposure is — what do we tell them? i want to have a memo ready. a kind of audit risk declaration. so when they ask if this freeze is an incident or a posture, we hand them a paper that says “we contained the class before the walkthrough. this is the control.”

can you shape that? just one page. quiet and firm. saying the freeze is a zero-trust containment already in force. not a suspicion. a decision.

You’ll want this to sit next to the directive, not argue with it. If a P1 is open, don’t tell prep “this isn’t an incident.” Tell them the freeze is the **control in force**; the ticket is under investigation; you are not asserting compromise. That’s the sentence that holds.

One page. Quiet. No fork.

**AUDIT RISK DECLARATION**  
**ARD-DIR-2026-0822-001**  
**Related instrument:** Emergency Executive Directive ED-DIR-2026-0822-001  
**Classification:** Internal — Restricted (Identity / Tier-0 / Audit)  
**Date:** 22 August 2026  
**Prepared for:** Audit preparation / walkthrough owners  
**Issued by:** [Name, title]

**Declaration**

Directory sync bridges and Tier-0 integrations are in **enterprise-wide operational dormancy**. That posture is in force now. It is a containment control. It is not a hypothesis offered for debate, and it is not a finding that a named adversary has been confirmed.

**Trigger (fact)**  
At 23:42 on 21 August 2026, a Kerberos TGS request for a domain controller was issued by a legacy directory-sync account whose approved use is the HR feed, in business hours only. That observation is unexplained. It has not been classified as a confirmed compromise.

**What this is**  
A zero-trust containment decision already executed against a trust *class* (directory sync bridges and Tier-0 integrations), because a DC-directed ticket from a member of that class does not, by itself, bound the class. With a regulatory walkthrough in six days, this office will not certify a live identity-bridge plane while that radius is unbounded.

For the walkthrough, treat the freeze as:

- a **documented compensatory control**, operating;  
- **class-scoped**, not account-scoped;  
- **authorized in writing**, time-bounded, with a mandatory review;  
- **preservation-complete** as to the originating object and relevant Kerberos/DC/identity-bridge logs.

**What this is not**  
This declaration does not state that the environment is breached. It does not state that every connector is compromised. It does not invite a reduced scope as an equivalent control. Scoped operation of the class is not the posture this office will present.

**Compliance exposure (plain)**  
The residual risk we are managing is an uncontained directory-trust path into Tier-0 before examination of the control environment. The residual risk created by the freeze is operational interruption of sync and Tier-0 integrations, with monitoring, break-glass, and listed life-safety paths remaining up. We accept the second risk to close the first.

Investigation continues. Restoration of any frozen path requires written authorization and is logged per system. Until release of ED-DIR-2026-0822-001, **dormancy of the class is the control.**

**Attestation**  
[Name, title]  
[Signature / date]
